topic: Is settling ticket 65's Flux falsification claim on this cluster worth doing at all, or should 64/65 be retired in favour of literature

topic: Is a computed semver bump institution-relative — strictest band, declared reference band, matrix, or rule-changes-only
then_recommendation: (i) compute against the strictest band and tag that, with (iii) the per-institution matrix published as supporting evidence.
alignment_evidence: Two owner statements pull opposite ways and neither is on this exact question. Against: 'the financial risk of 21707 doesn't seem sane to the same on every org, its proporiate to the org right?' (2026-08-19) — he rejects one figure applied identically across orgs. For: '22 whatever the best practice for implementing semvers says' (2026-08-22), and published semver practice is one version per artefact. This was also recorded with '[not directly answered this round; recorded per recommendation]' — no owner reply of any kind.
now_recommendation: Two numbers, not one. The publisher ships one global version computed at the strictest band (semver practice, one artefact one version, conservative for consumers), and the adopter's composed artefact carries its own bump computed against its own appetite band — which composition already makes possible and a marketplace makes necessary, since an adopter pins a composition, not a publisher's file. Promote the per-institution matrix from evidence to a normative output on the adopter side.
rationale: This is a real judgement call the owner never made, and the strictest-band-only shape has the same smell as the flat £21707 he rejected on sight: driftwood is told to take a major it never experiences. It may still be the right answer under his own semver-best-practice instruction — which is exactly why he should decide rather than inherit my note. Sharpest question: 'When ludlow's cage tightens and driftwood's does not, does the publisher ship a major that driftwood never experiences — or does each adopter's composed artefact carry its own bump?'
blast_radius: Medium. computed-semver spec.md's window+matrix rules (ticket 24), the publisher gate (27) and adopter gate (28), the composed-artefact version field, and every already-cut tag's justification.

topic: What replaces the removed ledger's OSCAL risk-object output — the cage, the procurement record, or both
then_recommendation: (i) the cage produces it.
alignment_evidence: The owner banned the ledger — 'there must never be an exemption ledger EVER... everything is codified' (2026-08-20) — but said nothing about where its machine-readable risk object should come from instead. The brief has no owner words on OSCAL output, procurement records, or the emission point. This was an assistant judgement recorded on a bare 'agree'.
now_recommendation: Both, same schema, two emitters. The cage emits the runtime risk object for anything running; the procurement record emits the pre-adoption one for a product being chosen — necessary because, under P028's reframing, a product can be degraded out of existence and never produce a cage at all, and because a regulator or an insurer needs the object before deployment, not after. Under the eco-system north star the OSCAL risk object is the tradeable artefact — the thing a publisher signs, an adopter pins, and a marketplace prices — so a single emission point tied to admission is too narrow.
rationale: Cage-produces-it was the convenient answer: it required no new emitter and closed the ticket. It is defensible for running workloads and silent for everything else. The owner should decide, because it determines whether the risk object is an operational by-product or the estate's exportable currency. Sharpest question: 'If a COTS product is caged until it cannot run, who emits its OSCAL risk object — the cage that never got a workload, or the procurement record that rejected it?'
blast_radius: Medium. The OSCAL emitter and its schema, cage.py's output surface, the procurement record's fields, coverage/baseline reporting in policy-composition, and any consumer that assumed one emission point.

topic: How verification works across six checkouts after the split — hub aggregates, each repo self-verifies, or platform ships the harness as a dependency
then_recommendation: (iii) platform ships the verify harness as a pinned dependency, with (i) hub aggregation as the fallback for cross-cutting checks.
alignment_evidence: '2 split everything. We are demonstrating a multi org thing' (2026-08-19), 'goes in all the repos its supposed to go in' (2026-08-25), and the standing honesty rule from the map, 'every verify script fails when it cannot see'. A harness each org pins and runs is the multi-org reading; a hub-side aggregator is the monorepo reading in new clothes.
now_recommendation: Decide honestly, because what shipped is the fallback, not the decision. The six orgs are real (each .estate-clone/<party> has an origin at github.com/policy-as-versioned-<party>/<party>, and estate/ really is gone from the hub, .gitignore'd). But verify/ and talk/ are still tracked directories in this hub repo rather than separate repos; verify/_estate.py points at a disposable .estate-clone/ that clone-estate.sh reassembles so the checks walk 'the same shape these checks always walked'; and no institution repo pins a platform harness — driftwood's workflows are shift-left, release, renovate-run, propose-tier, verify-identity-regexp and cut-release, none of them consuming one. The '28/28 green' number is therefore produced by a hub-side aggregator over a reassembled monorepo-shaped tree. Under the eco-system north star, a harness the platform publishes and each adopter pins is itself a product demonstration — an adopter proving its own compliance with a signed, versioned tool it chose to consume.
rationale: Candidly: (iii) was recorded, (i) was built, and the gap is exactly the kind of quiet reversion to convenience the owner is auditing for — it is also load-bearing for what '28/28 green' means to an audience. The owner should choose rather than discover it in a demo. Sharpest question: 'Is a hub-side aggregator over a reassembled six-repo checkout an honest multi-org verification, or must each org run a pinned harness and fail on its own?'
blast_radius: Large. verify/ and talk/ becoming real repos in the hub org, clone-estate.sh and _estate.py, the composition of the 28 beats and what the number claims, CI in all six org repos, and the dual-signing/pinning path the harness would need as a consumed dependency.

topic: Platform owns one corpus and generator; no institution owns a corpus (Round 2 Q1)
then_recommendation: Platform owns one corpus and one generator beside computed-semver/. Semver is a property of the artefact, not the consumer, so no institution owns a corpus; per-institution pre-adoption checks are ticket 05's problem, not a second corpus.
alignment_evidence: The brief cuts both ways and settles neither. For centralisation: nothing. Against it: '2 split everything. We are demonstrating a multi org thing' (2026-08-19) and 'the estate is split across independent organisations, with no shortcuts back to one org'. The owner has never been asked whether a buyer of a policy feed gets to re-derive the seller's number.
now_recommendation: Keep the publisher-side corpus as the thing that sets the tag, but treat the adopter-side question as open and answer it explicitly against the marketplace frame: publish the generator and the subject so any adopter org can re-run the spine against its own workloads and disagree with the tag in public. In a Bloomberg/Gartner-shaped feeds economy, an unverifiable rating is the product's weakest point, and 'trust the signed evidence' is a weaker answer than 'here is the tool, re-run it'.
rationale: Presented at the time as a settled consequence of ticket 02, which made it feel like bookkeeping rather than an architectural choice about where authority sits in the eco-system. It is the latter. Ask the owner: in the feeds marketplace, can an adopter org re-derive the publisher's version number against its own estate and publish a dissent — or does it only ever consume the publisher's signed verdict?
blast_radius: Medium. Publishing the generator for adopter re-runs is additive (a packaged entry point plus the subject tree). Genuine per-institution corpora that could move a tag would be large: four spines, four evidence chains, and ticket 02's 'semver is a property of the artefact' would have to be reopened.

topic: Generator enumerates per CEL expression (satisfied/violated/absent) with a version-pin axis, combined pairwise not fully (Round 2 Q2)
then_recommendation: Enumerate per CEL expression rather than per field — the field space is infinite, the expression space is finite — add a version-pin axis, and combine the axes pairwise rather than as a full cross product.
alignment_evidence: Per-expression enumeration is sound and unopposed. The pairwise half cuts the space for tractability, against an owner who has said 'nothing is a nice to have, you're either building it or your not' (2026-07-23), 'theres no rush for this, but it does have to be right and comprehensive' (2026-08-04) and, four days ago, 'i'm interested in coverage and depth more, and less in the speed' (2026-08-27). No owner quote endorses a covering array.
now_recommendation: Keep pairwise as the default — the full three-way cross is claimed at over four million pods and is genuinely not runnable through kyverno apply — but stop asserting that pairwise loses nothing. Run a bounded random sample of the three-way cross once, publish how many bumps it finds that pairwise missed (ideally zero), and cite that number in the evidence instead of the current one-sentence disclaimer.
rationale: This is the clearest place in the batch where the assistant's recommendation optimised for its own runtime and was accepted with a bare 'agree'. To its credit, coverage.py refuses a coverage percentage and prints the pairwise gap as a sentence plus two counts, which is the honest form of a cut. But a declared hole is still a hole, and this owner has spent a month rejecting exactly the move of declaring something adequate without measuring it. One line to ask him: is a declared pairwise hole acceptable in the number you sell to adopters, or must the gate sample the full cross to prove the pairs lose nothing?
blast_radius: Small to add the sampled check (a mode in corpus_generator.py plus two counts in coverage.py). Large if pairwise were abandoned entirely: the spine goes from 100 entries to an unrunnable population, and every cached evidence document and the CI regenerate-and-diff check would need rebuilding.

topic: Definition of 'shape' for the witness-miss check: per-expression outcome tuple plus pin-inside (Round 4 Q3)
then_recommendation: A shape is the tuple of outcomes each subject CEL expression gives on that pod, plus whether its pin is inside the version array. A witness is covered when its tuple already appears in the spine; cosmetic differences are ignored.
alignment_evidence: The brief has nothing directly on shape identity. The nearest owner statement is about cages as the variable: 'you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change' (2026-08-20) — which suggests a workload's cage tier is part of what distinguishes it, and this definition omits it.
now_recommendation: Reopen the definition against P060. When the tier label became a generated axis 30 minutes after this decision, the shape definition was never updated: witness-manifest.yaml's shape is still outcomes plus pin_inside with no tier. So a real workload whose only distinguishing property is the cage it lands in is declared 'covered' by a spine pod that shares its predicate outcomes and nothing else. Either add the effective tier to the tuple, or state in the evidence that witness coverage is a predicate-level claim only.
rationale: This is not a defect the owner caused; it is an inconsistency the session introduced by reversing itself mid-flight and never revisiting what the reversal touched. It is also currently untested in the only way that matters, since all six real witnesses return shape: null. One line to ask him: when the cage tier became an axis, did it become part of a workload's identity for coverage — or is coverage only ever a claim about predicates?
blast_radius: Small to medium: witness_set.py's shape tuple and its comparison, the witness manifest schema, and any regenerated evidence. It is a cheap fix now and an expensive one once real witnesses land and their recorded shapes have to be recomputed.

topic: Replace the residual axis with a tier-label axis (absent/baseline/restricted/quarantine), reversing Round 3 Q1
then_recommendation: Generate the tier label instead of a residual: absent, baseline, restricted, quarantine. No invented money; it matches what a pod actually carries, since cage-tier.yaml is a MutatingPolicy reading posture.acme.io/tier and the £ engine never enters admission. Drops the residual axis entirely.
alignment_evidence: The mechanism claim is true — graded/cage.py's select_tier(uncaged_ale, tolerance) runs upstream of admission, and only platform/wargamer/tier_pr.py writes the label, by proposing a PR. But the owner's spine is the opposite direction of travel: 'change the regulator financial fine we might get for a breach and ...' every control downstream re-proportions itself (2026-07-23); 'its never an exemption it'll be a informed caging based on risk appetite/threat intel' (2026-08-21); 'there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional' (2026-08-22). The price is the mechanism, not a decoration on it.
now_recommendation: Do not let the current implementation's boundary become the model's boundary. Under this decision a re-price that moves every driftwood workload from baseline to restricted — the exact demonstration the whole talk is built on — changes no policy text, so the computed version number does not move. P061 keeps select_tier under evidence as a separate pure-function check, but that check cannot bump the tag. Either bring the appetite bands and select_tier's mapping into the subject so a re-price is a policy release, or state explicitly and in the evidence that the £ to cage link is deliberately outside the version line and say what does carry it.
rationale: This is the batch's most consequential decision and the one where the assistant's argument was strongest-sounding and least examined. 'No invented money' was a genuine virtue — manufacturing a residual for Dex would have been fabrication of the kind the owner has repeatedly caught. But the recommendation quietly promoted an implementation limitation into a design principle, four days after the owner's own words made pricing the whole point of the cage, and sixteen days after he warned against exactly this ('a walking skeleton quietly becoming the ceiling'). One line to ask him: when a re-price moves a workload from baseline to restricted with no policy text changed, is that a policy version bump — or is the £ to cage link deliberately outside the version line?
blast_radius: Large if reversed. corpus_generator.py's tier axis and its two tier pairings, cage_engine.py's dial-spec permissiveness comparison, coverage.py's cells, the 100-file generated spine and its checksum, and all three signed evidence documents would regenerate; a residual or band axis would have to re-enter the corpus, reopening P047's institution-free entry and P061's split. It would also pull platform/risk/appetite.json and graded/cage.py into the versioned subject for the first time.

topic: Four unanswered uncertainties about what 'mash up' composition means (direction, what is inherited, whether override exists, whether the bump is even the point)
then_recommendation: None — an open clarifying question with no recommendation attached.
alignment_evidence: Two of the four were answered by the owner himself the same day and after: direction — 'the intent was never to inherit from tiself, it was to inherit from others' (2026-08-21); override — 'its never an exemption it'll be a informed caging based on risk appetite/threat intel' (2026-08-21). The fourth was never answered and is exactly what he stopped the build over: 'we seem to have drifted a fair way from thinking and original ambition' (2026-08-27), against a north star of 'one loosely coupled system but its a broader whole eco-system, with the orgs as an example consumers'.
now_recommendation: Ask uncertainty 4 properly, because it is the audit's own question in miniature. My recommendation: composition is the eco-system, and the semver gate is one consumer of it — not the reverse. Publishers (nist, ico, feeds, platform) publish; adopter orgs compose and are caged; the twin reads the composed graph as intelligence; the bump is a derived by-product that happens to be computable. Today the record has it the other way up: composition arrived as a sub-question of 'does inheritance earn its place in the version gate' (ticket 06), and it still carries that framing in the map. Re-parent it.
rationale: This is the sharpest item in the batch and the only one where a deferral genuinely cost something. I asked four good questions, got 'prototype what we now understand is needed', and treated that as licence to answer all four myself by building. Three of my implicit answers happen to hold up. The fourth — subordinating composition to the version gate — is a live candidate for the drift the owner has now stopped the build over, and it was my framing, not his.
blast_radius: Large if the fourth answer flips. The composition spec's problem statement, the map's dependency arrows, ADR-0011's seam ('the adopter gate computes the bump after composition'), the ordering of the demo, and the pitch narrative all currently present the gate as the destination and composition as the mechanism. Re-parenting is mostly narrative and spec surgery, but it changes which artefact is the product.

topic: What an expression no pod reached means: fail hard, allow silent exclusion, or a declared exclusion file
then_recommendation: Fail hard and name the expression. Add a declared exclusion file for genuinely unsatisfiable ones, each entry carrying a reason, printed in the evidence. Silence is never allowed.
alignment_evidence: Two of the owner's rules pull opposite ways here and neither is squarely on point. For: 'not allow scope to drop in this and prematurely declare things as done' (2026-08-05) — failing hard on an unreached expression is exactly that guard. Against: 'there must never be an exemption ledger EVER, this is a banned concept explicitly, everything is codified' (2026-08-20), said the day before this decision. A human-writable file of declared coverage holes is a ledger in shape even though it grants nothing.
now_recommendation: Keep failing hard. Put the sharp question to the owner rather than deciding it for him a second time. My own read: the exclusion file survives the ban because it is the inverse of an exemption — it grants no permission, it forces permanent disclosure, and P073's two-tier rule means no human can promote a hole to proved. If the owner disagrees, the alternative is not silence but hard failure with no escape at all, which is buildable today because coverage-exclusions.yaml is empty: every predicate in the real subject is genuinely reached.
rationale: The one-line question: 'you banned exemption ledgers outright — is a file of human-declared, permanently-printed coverage holes the thing you banned, or the disclosure you actually wanted?' I recommended this file one day after the categorical ban and never surfaced the collision, and my own ticket text even admits the risk ('an escape hatch that risks bringing curation back') without connecting it to his words. That is the failure mode this audit exists to catch.
blast_radius: Small today, precisely because the file is empty. platform/computed-semver/coverage-exclusions.yaml, the loader and static_proof in coverage.py, and their selfchecks. Removing the mechanism entirely costs perhaps a hundred lines and loses the safe-degradation property if CEL unreachability ever becomes provable in practice.

topic: What can fail the build: a coverage percentage threshold, or binary gates
then_recommendation: No percentage threshold ever. Three binary gates instead: an unreached predicate fails, a witness shape missing from the generated spine fails, movement traced to an unversioned policy fails. The pairwise gap never blocks, it is only stated.
alignment_evidence: '3 there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional' (2026-08-22) — said the morning after this decision. Also '5 you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change' (2026-08-20). The whole vocabulary of a thing that admits or refuses is what he moved off.
now_recommendation: Keep the three refusals for structural incoherence — an unreached predicate and a missing witness shape are defects in the measuring instrument, not policy verdicts, and refusing to publish a broken measurement is not a gate in the sense he abandoned. But put the real question to him: when a publisher's release is refused, does the refusal end there, or does it get priced and caged like everything else — publish the version at a degraded tier so adopters see a quarantined release rather than nothing at all? Under the marketplace north star the second is more interesting, because a feed that goes silent tells a subscriber less than a feed that publishes a downgraded rating.
rationale: One line to ask: 'you said there is no real gate anymore, just cages — does that apply to the publisher's release gate too, or only to admission?' The three binary gates are individually good and honest. What I never did was re-examine them after the owner dissolved the gate concept a few hours later; I carried on building refusal paths into ADR-0011 and the adopter gate because the tickets were already cut. That is ticket-closure momentum overriding a stated pivot.
blast_radius: Medium. platform/computed-semver/gate.py's refusal paths and its always-emit-signed-evidence-on-refusal behaviour, pairing.py and witness_set.py's failing checks, ADR-0011, the adopter gate wiring in shift-left CI (issue 28), and the composition spec's own refusal list, which uses the same vocabulary. Note the refusal path is already partly cage-shaped: the gate always emits and signs evidence even when it refuses, which is closer to a priced downgrade than to a closed door.

topic: Predicates vs variables: whether coverage is defined over predicate expressions only
then_recommendation: Define coverage over predicate expressions only (matchConditions and validations). A variable counts as covered when an enumerated axis spans its value space; uncovered variables (the cage dial, the container rewrite) are named in the not-looked-at list. Framed explicitly as a correction to ticket 03's wording, not a new axis.
alignment_evidence: 'nothing is a nice to have, you're either building it or your not' (2026-07-23) and 'you'll have to be careful to not allow scope to drop in this and prematurely declare things as done' (2026-08-05). The measurement definition was narrowed on the explicit ground that 'no new axis is added' — a tractability argument — and the one live thing it declines to measure is the cage dial, which by 2026-08-22 is the owner's whole enforcement model: 'It's the spec of the cage that can change'.
now_recommendation: Do not simply re-ratify. The substance is better than the framing suggests: the dial is not actually unmeasured, it is measured by cage_engine.py's Track 2, which compares cage specs on a permissiveness partial order and calls a less-permissive spec major. That is a stronger check than coverage would have been. But the ticket text tells the reader the dial is a hole, and the evidence's not-looked-at list does not even mention it because a mutation-only variable never becomes a coverage cell. Fix the disclosure so it states which mechanism measures what, and put the narrowing to the owner rather than letting it stand on my convenience argument.
rationale: One line to ask: 'coverage deliberately does not measure the cage dial — are you content that cage-spec comparison covers it, or must the dial's value space be enumerated too?' Candidly, 'this is a correction to wording, not a new axis' is the sentence of someone avoiding work. It happens to be defensible because another mechanism picked up the slack, but I did not justify it that way at the time — I justified it by what would be cheap.
blast_radius: Small to widen, small to reverse. coverage.py's is_bare_variable / axis_spans_variable path and its selfcheck, the not-looked-at entries in evidence/*.json, .scratch/computed-semver/issues/04 and 23. Adding a dial axis would touch corpus_generator.py's pairwise builder and regenerate the spine.

topic: Where the declared bump is read from (cut-release.yml workflow input vs versions.yaml vs PR title)
then_recommendation: Read the declared bump from cut-release.yml's version input and gate before git tag; keep a cheaper second check in release.yml verifying the signed evidence matches the tag.
alignment_evidence: Nothing in the brief speaks to where a version input lives. The nearest owner words cut both ways: 'whatever the best practice for implementing semvers says' (2026-08-22) argues for a declared version in a repo file, while 'the shared, and regularots should be real' (2026-07-23) and 'you do whatever you need to do using my gh cli creds' (2026-08-15) show he is content for GitHub to be the substrate. He has never said the eco-system must survive off GitHub.
now_recommendation: Move the declared bump into a versioned file in the repo (versions.yaml or equivalent), with cut-release.yml reading it rather than owning it. Under the eco-system north star the publishers are not all the platform team — regulators like ico and nist publish into the same marketplace, and binding the declaration of intent to one CI vendor's workflow input makes the gate a GitHub feature rather than a property of the policy artefact. A file-held declaration is also reviewable in the PR that proposes it, which the workflow input is not.
rationale: Candidly: this recommendation optimised for where the assistant's existing plumbing already sat. cut-release.yml existed, so gating its input was the shortest diff, and the second check in release.yml was added to cover the seam that choice opened. That is a real cost — the declared bump is now un-reviewable before it is used, which sits badly with 'with code reviews gating completion' (2026-08-20). Sharpest question to ask him: 'When a regulator publishes a policy version from something that isn't GitHub Actions, where does its declared bump live?'
blast_radius: Small-medium. cut-release.yml and release.yml in platform plus the three institutions, the gate's entry point, and ticket 13's multi-tag work. No change to the engine. A day's work, not a redesign.

topic: Whether the adopter's gate fails the Renovate PR when its composed bump disagrees with the publisher's tag, or only reports
then_recommendation: Fail the PR when the composed bump is major; only report otherwise. Print both bumps side by side in the PR body.
alignment_evidence: '3 there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional' (2026-08-22, the same day). '5 you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change' (2026-08-20). And his own account today: 'my thoughts through grilling sessions did evolve though from binary admission to cage/constraint shape and around risk assessment was done and what we modelled'. A hard threshold at the letter 'major' is the binary admission shape he spent that week moving off.
now_recommendation: Grade the adopter's response by priced impact on that org, not by the letter of the bump. Under the one-£-currency north star the adopter already knows what a verdict movement costs it: a minor with a large £ exposure for driftwood deserves more than a comment, and a major that touches nothing driftwood runs deserves less than a block. The composed bump should set the cage the incoming version lands in — degrading toward unmergeable as the priced impact rises — with the letter shown as evidence rather than used as the trigger.
rationale: Candidly, this is the weakest recommendation in the batch and it was mine. 'Fail on major, report otherwise' is the demo-legible answer — one red PR on stage, everything else green — and it was cheap, a single comparison. It reproduces exactly the binary he had already abandoned, in the one place where the adopter's own priced view of the change is available and unused. Sharpest question to ask him: 'Should the adopter's PR response be graded by the £ impact on that org, rather than by whether the letter says major?'
blast_radius: Medium. The disagreement branch in all three adopter gates (driftwood 889, ludlow 1021, tuppence 482 lines), the PR body rendering in ticket 29, and a new dependency from the adopter gate onto the FAIR/currency layer that does not exist today. The engine and publisher side are untouched.

topic: Q4 - what makes a change major when the cage is the only enforcement
then_recommendation: (b) The movement rule: any downward move of any cage dial is major, with no estimate of whether a workload survives it. Viability rules need a threshold, and cs-04 banned thresholds.
alignment_evidence: The premise moved under the owner the same week: `3 there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional` (2026-08-22) and `you’re always caged even if it’s a permissive one. It’s the spec of the cage that can change` (2026-08-20). But also `its never an exemption it'll be a informed caging based on risk appetite/threat intel` (2026-08-21) — an 'informed' cage is priced, and the movement rule prices nothing.
now_recommendation: Keep the movement rule as the version classifier — falsifiable and threshold-free — but stop letting it be the whole answer. Every computed downward move should carry the £ cost of that move, from verify/proportionality/render.py and ultimately the twin, into the signed evidence. That is the counter-pressure named limit 9.1 admits does not exist, and the only thing that makes 'informed caging' true rather than a phrase.
rationale: Defensible, and the alternative was worse, but it was taken inside a versioning ticket and quietly settled an enforcement question the owner was still evolving. The gate now labels the ratchet and has no opinion on it, as the answer document concedes. Sharpest question: 'Should a release that tightens the cage be refusable when the twin prices the tightening above the org's risk appetite, or is the version number all the gate ever gets to say?'
blast_radius: Medium. cage_engine.py, the bump classification of every signed release, and the evidence schema if £ is added. Adding £ is additive; redefining major is not, and would re-classify the shipped 2.0.0/3.0.0 pair.

topic: Does removing an enforcement surface get its own gate axis, or only a named limit
then_recommendation: (b) the release gate refuses outright any release that removes an enforcement surface from a version - a structural refusal, not a bump class; leave 'major' as defined.
alignment_evidence: Owner, 2026-08-20: 'nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive' and 'you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change'. Sharpest question for the owner: 'If there is no real gate any more, only cages, should a release that loosens a cage be refused - or priced, so the balance sheet refuses it instead?'

topic: Canonical control id form (bare 'ac-6' vs prefixed 'nist-800-53:ac-6' vs display 'AC-6')
then_recommendation: Use the bare catalogue id exactly as the catalogue writes it ('ac-6'); the source prefix is duplicated state because the enclosing source/href already names the catalogue; display labels never become keys.
alignment_evidence: Nothing in the brief speaks to control-id syntax. The nearest on-point owner words are about not inventing conventions locally: '22 whatever the best practice for implementing semvers says' (2026-08-22) — which supports taking the catalogue's own form. Against it, the orchestrator's arc records the owner reframing policy as ordinary code with 'multiple simultaneous regulators and customer SLAs' (Phase 4 summary, paraphrase not a quote), which is where a bare id stops being unique. No owner quote either way.
now_recommendation: Keep the bare catalogue form as the wire value, but make the key a (source, id) pair wherever a claim can name more than one catalogue — the composed header already lists parents by party+kind+sha, so bind each control claim to the parent it resolved against. Under the feeds-marketplace north star an adopter will one day compose NIST controls, an ICO catalogue and a customer SLA catalogue in the same set, and 'ac-6' will collide.
rationale: The then-recommendation is correct today and only today: it holds while exactly one catalogue is in scope per claim context. The justification given ('the catalogue is already named by the enclosing source/href') is an argument about the current file layout, not about the eco-system the owner is aiming at — publishers plural, feeds plural, regulators plural. That is a real design question the owner should answer rather than inherit from a file-shape argument. Sharpest question to ask: 'When driftwood composes NIST 800-53, an ICO catalogue and a customer SLA catalogue at once, what tells two different ac-6s apart — and is that the composed header, or the id itself?'
blast_radius: Small-to-medium. platform/compose/composition.py resolver, platform control-claim files (ticket 10 rewrote them to bare ids), the three adopters' composed/ trees and HEADER.yaml hole lists (~577 ids each), .scratch/policy-composition/issues/03 and 10, ADR-0013. topic: What happens to a baseline control nothing implements (absolute hole count vs new-hole-only refusal)
then_recommendation: Do not refuse on the absolute hole count; refuse only on a NEW hole relative to the previously composed set, printing the count and the hole ids — an old hole is tracked debt, a new hole is a refusal.
alignment_evidence: The whole refuse / don't-refuse framing is a gate framing, and the owner had already dissolved gates two days earlier: '3 there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional' (2026-08-22), and 'its never an exemption it'll be a informed caging based on risk appetite/threat intel' (2026-08-21). Cutting the other way, he does accept build-time gates: 'with code reviews gating completion' (2026-08-20). The layer this applies to is genuinely unsettled in his own words.
now_recommendation: Price the holes rather than count them. Each unimplemented baseline control carries a £ exposure via the ico pricing feed; the composed artefact should carry priced holes and a total, and the refusal threshold should be a £ figure against the adopter's declared risk appetite, not a set-difference. A new hole that prices at nothing should not stop a composition; an old hole that re-prices upward when a regulator publishes a bigger fine should — and today nothing makes that happen.
rationale: Candidly: this recommendation exists to make P124 shippable. MODERATE with 285 (in fact ~577) holes is only tolerable because this rule declares them pre-existing debt, so the estate could close the ticket green. That is ticket-closure logic, not risk logic. It also encodes a binary refusal at exactly the layer the owner spent August converting into graded, priced cages, and it is the one place where his 'no real gate' doctrine and his 'code reviews gating completion' constraint genuinely conflict. Sharpest question to ask: 'Does no-gate-only-cages apply to the composition check too — should a new hole refuse the build, or price the cage?'
blast_radius: Medium. compute_holes and the previous-header comparison in platform/compose/composition.py, the composed/HEADER.yaml holes block in all three adopter repos, compose-check in each adopter's CI, ADR-0013, spec.md, tickets 14 and 18. Adding pricing pulls in the ico pricing parent and the £ engine, which is the larger part.

topic: Which proposer raises the cage-tier drift
then_recommendation: Extend the existing war-gamer with a tier-drift row rather than build a separate composition proposer — reuse the estate's engines, and avoid a second thing proposer_bounds.py must bound.
alignment_evidence: No owner words on which component proposes a tier. Adjacent: the arc records governance being demoted to 'one enactment arm' of the twin (Phase 3), and the owner's ambition for 'a whole economic platform and model for risk feeds' (2026-08-19) — both of which put the intelligence upstream of the estate. Under the eco-system north star the twin is the intelligence and the estate is enactment: a cage tier is a risk decision, so the twin's Monte Carlo model should produce the number and the estate war-gamer should carry it into a PR. Today the tier heuristic lives entirely in the estate and the twin is not consulted at all.
rationale: The reuse argument is sound engineering and the decision is cheap to keep. What was never put to the owner is the layering question underneath it — whether the estate should be deciding tiers at all, or enacting a tier the twin computed. That is the seam between the two halves of his system, and it was settled by a convenience argument about how many things proposer_bounds.py has to bound. topic: Whether each adopter keeps its own rejection ledger or all write the shared platform ledger
then_recommendation: Each adopter keeps its own — a rejection is that adopter's editorial history and platform must not hold per-adopter state it cannot verify. Cost: adopters do not learn from each other's rejections, which nothing did anyway.
alignment_evidence: Nothing in the brief addresses the ledger's location. Two owner absolutes bear on its existence, not its placement: 2026-08-20 'there must never be an exemption ledger EVER, this is a banned concept explicitly, everything is codified' and 2026-08-21 'its never an exemption it'll be a informed caging based on risk appetite/threat intel'.
now_recommendation: Do not settle placement until the ledger's identity is settled. If the file only records 'this proposal was declined, do not re-raise it for N hours' it is a flood guard and per-adopter is right. If it accumulates 'we decided not to tighten this cage' it is a register of accepted risk sitting outside the codified policy — the shape the owner banned by name. Ask him. If it is the second kind, the answer is neither location: a declined tightening becomes a codified informed cage in the party artefact, priced, and there is no ledger.
rationale: Sharpest question to put to him: 'Is proposer_bounds.py's rejection ledger a flood guard, or is it a list of tightenings you chose not to make — and if it is the second, how is that not the exemption ledger you banned?' I framed this in August as a storage-location question and never asked what the file is, which is the only question that matters.
blast_radius: Small if it stays a flood guard (one path, one fixture). Large if it turns out to be an accepted-risk register: the concept is deleted, proposer_bounds.py's dedupe is rebuilt on the branch name, and every declined tightening has to become a codified cage entry in three adopter repos.

topic: The legal route for an adopter that wants a stricter cage, given a subclass cannot restate a mutate or a generate
then_recommendation: Only the proposer: overlay restatement stays ValidatingPolicy-only, and a stricter cage reaches the adopter as a tier label set upstream via ADR-0015's proposer, as a reviewed PR. Landed as ADR-0016.
alignment_evidence: Owner 2026-08-21: 'the intent was never to inherit from tiself, it was to inherit from others and allow for policy like any other dpeendency to be a mash up like an object orienta[ted]' — in the OO model he named, a subclass tightening its parent is the ordinary move, not the forbidden one. ADR-0013's 'selection is the risk-bearing act' makes the adopter the risk-bearer; this decision leaves the risk-bearer unable to be stricter than its publisher until a feed prices it so.
now_recommendation: Re-open. In an eco-system, an adopter org must be able to be stricter than its publisher on its own authority — that is the whole reason a subscriber is not a tenant. Either the overlay can carry a tier floor the adopter sets itself (a value it may only move in the tightening direction, so it can never be an exemption), or ADR-0016's no-restating-a-mutate rule needs an exception for tightening. What must not stand is 'the only route to being stricter is to wait for the price to agree with you'.
rationale: Sharpest question: 'Can driftwood decide to be stricter than platform without waiting for a feed to price it that way — and if not, in what sense is the adopter the risk-bearer?' Two extra reasons to distrust the record here: the recommendation was the option that needed no new machinery, and the owner's reply is not present as a user turn at all — the digest marks it accepted by inference from an AskUserQuestion result, which is the weakest consent in this batch.
blast_radius: Medium. ADR-0016 gains an exception or a companion, the overlay schema gains a tightening-only field, party_artefact.py's validation and self-check change, compose.py's render changes, and all three adopter party.yaml files gain a field. The 'a subclass never restates a mutate' line in CONTEXT.md is rewritten.

topic: Whose problem undeclared mutate-before-validate ordering is, between composed members
then_recommendation: Platform machinery, out of scope — rely on Kyverno's webhook ordering guarantee that mutates run before validates, record the residual risk, and rule the question out of scope for the ticket.
alignment_evidence: Owner 2026-08-05: 'not allow scope to drop in this and prematurely declare things as done'; 2026-07-23: 'nothing is a nice to have, you're either building it or your not'. My then-recommendation converted a correctness question into a documentation entry so the ticket could close, and bundled a defensible half (validate ordering) with an undefended half (mutate ordering) under one 'out of scope'.

topic: Which control ids an adopter may add — only ids resolving in a catalogue it already inherits, or also ids it invents for a rule of its own
then_recommendation: (a) Catalogue ids only — ADR-0013 makes an id absent from the catalogue a hard failure; a company-specific rule is a policy, not a control, and composes through the overlay with no catalogue id.
alignment_evidence: Never answered, never re-put; settled by ADR-0013's existing hard-fail. The owner's standing absolutes pull both ways and neither is squarely on point: 'all of this is the policy we're not carving exemptions ... we're codifying how the organisation operates' (2026-07-31) argues everything must be expressible; nothing in the brief says a bespoke rule must carry a catalogue id.
now_recommendation: Re-open, because of what it does to the balance sheet rather than to the schema. Coverage and holes are computed over control ids; a rule with no id is invisible to coverage, so its absence is never a hole and never gets priced. Under the one-£-currency north star, a bespoke control that driftwood decides it needs, and then fails to implement, must show up as an unpriced gap somewhere. Either bespoke ids are admissible in a namespaced form, or the pricing path needs a second input for policy-space obligations that control-space cannot name.

I answered this in August as a schema-validation question. It is a pricing-coverage question, and I never traced it to the £.
blast_radius: Medium to large. Admitting namespaced bespoke ids touches the catalogue resolution in compose.py, the coverage and hole computation, ADR-0013's hard-fail rule, the composed-artefact schema, and the ico pricing join. Leaving it and adding a second pricing input touches the FAIR path instead.

topic: Does shipping an implementation make the adopter an implementations publisher
then_recommendation: No new obligation. The adopter's member is an overlay member of the composed artefact ADR-0012 already makes it gitsign-sign; no separate semver axis, no separate pin. It becomes an implementations publisher only when another party pins its composed artefact — a fact about the pinner, not a role to declare.
alignment_evidence: The composition shape is the owner's own correction: 'the intent was never to inherit from tiself, it was to inherit from others and allow for policy like any other dpeendency to be a mash up like an object orienta[tion]' (2026-08-21). But today's steer is broader than composition mechanics: 'one loosely coupled system but its a broader whole eco-system, with the orgs as an example consumers to demonstrate the whole eco-system operating', and 'we've developed a reference arch, and a platform but also a whole economic platform and model for risk feeds' (2026-08-19). The brief has no owner words on publisher registration either way.
now_recommendation: Keep the no-extra-obligation rule — it is correct and it kills ceremony. But add what the marketplace needs and this decision quietly cut: a way for a party to declare itself a publisher so others can find it. Today publisherhood is retroactive and invisible; nobody can browse for a publisher, only discover one by already having pinned it. A Bloomberg-terminal-for-risk-feeds needs a catalogue entry, not an inference. That is additive — a discovery record next to the party artefact, not a new obligation on the artefact itself.
rationale: Candidly: the assistant answered the narrow engineering question (does this add a versioning burden?) and treated the role question as settled by it. It was not. 'A fact about the pinner' is a tidy formulation that happens to require zero new machinery — which is why it went unchallenged. Against the eco-system north star it is a real narrowing: a marketplace with no publisher directory is not a marketplace. Sharpest question to ask: 'In the feeds marketplace, should a party be able to publish itself as available to pin, or is being pinned by someone who already knew about you the only way to become a publisher?'
blast_radius: Small-to-medium if extended (not reversed). ADR-0017's closing clause, ticket 07, CONTEXT.md's role terms; plus one new discovery surface in the hub org. Nothing in the composition engine, the pricing path or the signed artefacts changes — the addition sits beside them.

topic: What refuses at composition time for namespace declarations (new-versus-recorded on ungoverned namespaces)
then_recommendation: (a) A namespace carrying the institution label but not governed:"true" refuses at merge time, using ticket 03's new-versus-recorded rule, so a brownfield estate records an existing ungoverned namespace but refuses a new one. (b) is moot; out-of-band cluster drift is (d).
alignment_evidence: 'nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive' (2026-08-20) and 'you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change' (2026-08-20). A recorded pre-existing ungoverned namespace runs everything inside it uncaged, indefinitely, at no price. And 'there must never be an exemption ledger EVER, this is a banned concept explicitly, everything is codified' (2026-08-20) — a durable recorded list of namespaces the rules do not reach is functionally that ledger, whatever it is called.
now_recommendation: Keep the refusal on a new ungoverned namespace, but stop treating the recorded ones as free. Every pre-existing ungoverned namespace should carry a priced hole in the evidence document, proportionate to the workloads inside it, that appears on the balance sheet and grows the longer it stands — an informed cage on the namespace, exactly as the owner described. ADR-0018 currently says the first composition 'records three ungoverned namespaces and refuses on none' and then nothing else happens to them; that is a grandfather clause with no clock and no £, which is the one shape he banned by name.
rationale: The new-versus-recorded rule was inherited wholesale from ticket 03 because it was already built — reuse, not judgement. It is right for holes in a control set, where the cage downstream does price the gap. It is wrong for namespaces, where nothing downstream prices anything: the whole point of an ungoverned namespace is that no rule reaches into it. The assistant applied a familiar pattern past its domain and the owner said 'accept' three days after telling it exemptions were banned. Sharpest question: 'A recorded pre-existing ungoverned namespace is a carve-out nothing prices and nothing expires — how is that not the exemption ledger you banned, and should it not be a priced cage that gets more expensive the longer it stands?'
blast_radius: Medium. ADR-0018 point 3, ticket 15's lint (shipped), the evidence document's ungoverned list and its status field, the pricing path in ticket 16, and the three adopter Namespace manifests. Adding a price is additive to the lint rather than a rewrite of it — the refusal branch stays; what changes is what happens to the recorded ones.

topic: Widen orphan-guard's Deny-mode admission gate to cover the two Crossplane CRD types, closing the unlabeled-cloud-resource bypass
then_recommendation: Yes, extend the guard's scope — it matches the guard's own documented design intent, 'locked door, not opt-in door'.

It's the spec of the cage that can change' and 'nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive' (2026-08-20), then 'there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional' (2026-08-22).

Two verifiable holes today: (1) composed/orphan-guard.yaml matches resources ['pods'] only, hardcoded in platform/distribution/render-orphan-guard.py, and its matchCondition is has-policy-version-label — so a pod with no label is unmatched, which is an opt-in door, the exact shape P174 closed; (2) platform/graded/README.md states outright that 'A pod claiming no policy version at all (system/COTS) is out of scope, unmatched. Never denies.' Under 'nothing runs uncaged', an unlabelled pod should land in the loosest cage by default, not outside the model. Closing it changes render-orphan-guard.py and the composed orphan-guard in three adopter orgs, cage-tier.yaml's match conditions, the graded README's stated contract, the govern-what-you-dont-control COTS shim's boundary, and every capture showing an uncaged system pod.

then_recommendation: Enable it on the fleet repo only — closes ticket 09's automation gap, acknowledged as mildly loosening posture since any fleet workflow could then open PRs.

topic: Flagship as a real org's documented history (backtest spine) wearing a synthetic behavioural substrate
